newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir restores comupter link to Earth after break.
newsitem.headline: Mir restores comupter link to Earth after break.

text.p: Russia's Mission Control and the crew of the damaged Mir space station restored on Thursday a vital computer link which would allow experts to analyse data and help the cosmonauts repair the craft.

"We have received telemetry of a good quality and we are recording it now," said one of the experts as the screens of the computers, dead since the station lost most of its energy early in the day, came alive. The link-up ended with a "Go to sleep, good luck" message from Earth.

The latest problem hit Mir during the night from Wednesday to Thursday when one of the three-man Russian-U.S. crew mistakenly pulled out a vital computer cable, disrupting the power supply system and plunging the ship into its worst crisis since a near-fatal collision on June 25.

The power loss forced the crew to switch off most of Mir's systems, including light, heating and life-support systems on the main station. The cosmonauts had to to sit in their Soyuz escape capsule to communicate with Earth by radio.

Mission doctor Igor Goncharov later told Reuters the crew had succeeded in accumulating sufficient solar power in Mir's batteries to re-start the gyroscopic guidance system that keeps the panels lined up on the Sun.
The accumulated energy appeared to make it possible for the crew to restore the computer link.
